hunks.baseline: Just as the words said, it was a place of utter death.
hunks.sol: Just as the name said, a place utterly devoid of life.

hunks.baseline: The truth I hadn’t noticed until then came upon me all at once, cold as a blade pressed to the back of my neck.
hunks.sol: The truth I’d failed to notice came over me with the chill of a blade pressed to the back of my neck.

hunks.baseline: *How can there be no living things at all? How is this possible?*
hunks.sol: *No living things at all? How is that possible?*

hunks.baseline: The question sprang into my mind on instinct, but I quickly swallowed it down.
hunks.sol: I swallowed the question almost as soon as it sprang to mind.

hunks.baseline: A foolish question.
hunks.sol: It was a foolish question.

hunks.baseline: If the Lord of Heaven—no, the Demon King Asmodeus—stood at the beginning and end of all this, then it was even less surprising.
hunks.sol: Especially if the one behind all this was the Lord of Heaven—no, the Demon King Asmodeus.

hunks.baseline: The being who had dragged the apocalypse from the realm of imagination into reality.
From the moment I realized what he was, the word *common sense* had lost all meaning.
hunks.sol: He’d dragged an apocalypse that had existed only in people’s imaginations into reality. From the moment I learned what he was, *common sense* had lost all meaning.

hunks.baseline: So the question that quickly took the place of the first was a different one.
A more practical question, closer to the heart of the matter.
hunks.sol: Another question quickly took the first one’s place. One that was more practical, and closer to the heart of the matter.

hunks.baseline: I stared silently out the window at the empty landscape. Not a single bird called. Not an insect chirped. Then I spoke.
hunks.sol: I stared out the window. Not a bird called. Not an insect chirped.

hunks.baseline: It was far too late to ask how this could happen.
hunks.sol: It was far too late to ask *how*.

hunks.baseline: And it seemed the person hiding in the sandstorm that had blown in from far away, whose presence had settled on the carriage roof a moment earlier, knew that too.
hunks.sol: And it seemed the person who’d arrived with the sandstorm from afar and settled on the carriage roof a moment ago knew that too.

hunks.baseline: “Must be one of two things.”
hunks.sol: “One of two things.”

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint continued in a voice young enough to belong to a boy, yet bleak enough to betray the years he’d lived.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint’s voice was boyishly young, yet carried a bleakness that spoke of all the years he’d lived.

hunks.baseline: “The first is a final battle. One last fight, drawing on everything in Xinjiang.”
hunks.sol: “The first is a final battle. Gathering everything in Xinjiang for one last fight.”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know exactly what’s happened, but this whole region has lost its life force. People and animals have legs, so it would make sense if they disappeared. But even every plant in the area has withered away. Dark Heaven’s probably behind it.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know exactly what happened, but the whole of Xinjiang has lost the breath of life. People and animals have legs; they could have gone elsewhere. But even the plants across the region have withered. Dark Heaven’s probably behind it.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang took up the conversation in a gruff tone.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang cut in gruffly.

hunks.baseline: “You were eavesdropping like a rat, and all you’ve got is something anyone could’ve said.”
hunks.sol: “Eavesdropping like a rat, only to tell us something that goes without saying.”

hunks.baseline: “Watch your mouth. You never know. That rat might cut your throat tonight.”
hunks.sol: “Watch your mouth. That rat might cut your throat tonight.”

hunks.baseline: “I wouldn’t mind. We’re running low on food anyway. A nice, crisp roast rat would make a fine breakfast tomorrow.”
hunks.sol: “I wouldn’t mind. We’re running low on food. Roast rat, nice and crisp, would make a fine breakfast tomorrow.”

hunks.baseline: “There’s no hope that way of talking will ever improve. What the hell happened to all the years you’ve lived?”
hunks.sol: “That mouth of yours never gets any better. What the hell have you done with all the years you’ve lived?”

hunks.baseline: A shadow fell by the window as he answered flatly.

Like a ghost with no substance, the Slaughter Saint passed through the window as if it weren’t there and entered the carriage. He stared at me as though he could see straight through whatever I was hiding.
hunks.sol: A shadow fell across the window. The Slaughter Saint passed through it as though he had no substance, like a ghost, and entered the carriage. He stared at me as if he could see straight through what I was hiding.

hunks.baseline: I’d been traveling with the Slaughter Saint for quite a while, but this was the first time I’d been away for a whole month.
hunks.sol: I’d been traveling with the Slaughter Saint for quite a while, but this was the first time I’d been gone for a whole month. And by any ordinary measure, no one could sleep for an entire month.

hunks.baseline: And by ordinary standards, no one in the world could sleep for an entire month.
But what could I do?
The day would come when I’d tell him the truth myself. For now, though, I had to put on a straight face and bluff.
hunks.sol: But what could I do? The day would come when I told him the truth myself. For now, I’d have to bluff with a straight face.

hunks.baseline: “Yeah, I’ve always been a heavy sleeper.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah, I sleep a lot.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve got a special constitution.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve got an unusual constitution.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve wandered the land for fifty years, meeting all kinds of patients, and I’ve never encountered a constitution like that.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve wandered the land for fifty years and seen all kinds of patients. No such constitution exists.”

hunks.baseline: “Congratulations. You’ve discovered a new one after fifty years.”
hunks.sol: “Congratulations. After fifty years, you’ve discovered a new one.”

hunks.baseline: For a moment, suffocating silence filled the carriage.
The Slaughter Saint and even Jeok Cheongang stared at me as if I were a madman.
hunks.sol: A suffocating silence filled the carriage. The Slaughter Saint and even Jeok Cheongang stared at me as if I were a madman.

hunks.baseline: Fair enough. It was nonsense that didn’t even require medical knowledge to debunk.
hunks.sol: Fair enough. You didn’t need medical training to know that was nonsense.

hunks.baseline: “I’m kidding. Actually, I woke up a few times in between. You still have to take care of basic bodily functions and all that.”
hunks.sol: “I’m kidding. I did wake up a few times in between. You know, to take care of basic bodily functions and all that.”

hunks.baseline: “You wouldn’t. Only my Master knew. Right?”
hunks.sol: “Of course not. Only Master knew. Right?”

hunks.baseline: His reaction was a little odd, but when you’re lying, the important thing is to sound natural.
hunks.sol: His reaction was a little odd, but the most important thing when lying was to sound natural. I kept talking before the Slaughter Saint could notice.

hunks.baseline: I quickly continued before the Slaughter Saint could notice anything strange.

hunks.baseline: “I woke up once a few days ago, too. After sleeping so long, I had to pee and got hungry.”
hunks.sol: “I woke up once a few days ago, too. After sleeping so long, I had to pee, and I was hungry.”

hunks.baseline: “When exactly do you mean by a few days ago?”
hunks.sol: “When exactly was that?”

terminology_alerts.message: preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “Um… I wasn’t fully awake, so I’m not sure.”
hunks.sol: “Um… I wasn’t fully awake, so I don’t really know.”

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint nodded as if he understood, then muttered to himself.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint nodded, then muttered as if to himself.

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. Weird, isn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. Strange, isn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: “There’s something even stranger. Want to know what it is?”
hunks.sol: “Something even stranger happened. Would you like to hear it?”

hunks.baseline: Was it just my imagination, or had the air gone a little stale?
hunks.sol: Was it my imagination, or had the air turned a little murky?

hunks.baseline: I shook my head, uneasy for some reason.
hunks.sol: Uneasy for some reason, I shook my head.

hunks.baseline: “…No. Not particularly.”
hunks.sol: “…No. Not really.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s a good saying. But there’s another one that fits this situation better.”
hunks.sol: “A good saying. But another one fits this situation better.”

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint added in a gentle voice unlike his usual one, which made it feel all the more ominous.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint’s voice was gentler than usual, which made it all the more ominous.

hunks.baseline: “Keep talking and you’ll get a beating.”
hunks.sol: “That mouth of yours is asking for a beating.”

hunks.baseline: What do I think? What am I supposed to think?
hunks.sol: What was I supposed to think?

hunks.baseline: I forced a smile and answered.
hunks.sol: I forced a smile.

hunks.baseline: “I’m suddenly very curious. I’d love to hear this strange story.”
hunks.sol: “Now I’m very curious. I’d love to hear what happened.”

hunks.baseline: “On its own, it’s not that remarkable. To be exact, from my perspective, it was just a real nuisance.”
hunks.sol: “Taken on its own, it’s nothing remarkable. From where I stood, it was mostly a nuisance.”

hunks.baseline: “Quite the bond between Master and Disciple. From the very first morning after we set out, that ill-tempered old man made a racket if I didn’t check on you every morning and evening. Not a single day went by in peace.”
hunks.sol: “What a close Master and Disciple you are. From the first day of our journey, a certain ill-tempered old man raised hell unless I checked on you morning and evening. Not a single day went by in peace.”

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint’s eyes sank as he glared at Jeok Cheongang, as though just remembering it exhausted him.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint glared at Jeok Cheongang, looking exhausted just from remembering it.

hunks.baseline: “Lately, his damn fits have gotten worse than ever. You hadn’t woken up in nearly a month, so it was obvious something was wrong. He kept yelling at me, demanding to know why I hadn’t found the problem.”
hunks.sol: “Lately, his fits reached new heights. You’d been asleep for nearly a month, so he decided something must be wrong. He shouted at me, demanding to know why I couldn’t find the problem.”

hunks.baseline: “That was just two days ago. Got anything to say?”
hunks.sol: “That was only two days ago. Anything to say?”

hunks.baseline: Of course I don’t.
hunks.sol: Of course I had nothing.

hunks.baseline: I’d thought something felt off. Now I knew why Jeok Cheongang had acted so strangely earlier.
hunks.sol: I knew something had felt off. Now I understood Jeok Cheongang’s strange reaction earlier.

hunks.baseline: With the Slaughter Saint’s eyes on him—and mine too—Jeok Cheongang stared out the window and muttered,
hunks.sol: Under the Slaughter Saint’s stare—and mine—Jeok Cheongang looked out the window and muttered, “Well, I didn’t shout *that* much…”

hunks.baseline: “Well, I didn’t yell quite that much…”
“He even called me a quack.”
hunks.sol: “You even called me a quack.”

hunks.baseline: “I didn’t insult you quite that directly…”
hunks.sol: “I didn’t put it quite that directly…”

hunks.baseline: “Right. Now that I think about it, you did put it more gently. You asked if I’d learned medicine at a gambling den.”
hunks.sol: “True. You were a little more roundabout. You asked if I’d learned medicine at a gambling den.”

hunks.baseline: “I did say that, but it wasn’t that harsh…”
hunks.sol: “I did say that, but it wasn’t so harsh…”

hunks.baseline: “Hmm. I suppose I did go too far there. My pride won’t let me apologize, so I’ll offer my sincere regrets instead.”
hunks.sol: “Hmm. I suppose I went too far there. My pride won’t let me apologize, so I’ll offer my regrets instead.”

hunks.baseline: The answer was steeped in the essence of the Fire Gate Clan—a clan that had been making Murim’s people furious on a regular basis for more than three hundred years. A sound almost escaped me.
hunks.sol: It was an answer steeped in the essence of the Fire Gate Clan, which had spent over three hundred years regularly infuriating the martial artists of Murim. A sound of admiration nearly escaped me.

hunks.baseline: Almost. Then I saw the Slaughter Saint’s expression and held it back with every bit of strength I had.
hunks.sol: Then I saw the Slaughter Saint’s expression and held it in with everything I had.

hunks.baseline: If he’d seen this, he would’ve spouted some nonsense like, *Wow! I’ve never seen the greatest assassin of all time swear before!* Then I would’ve had to watch the greatest assassin of all time lose his temper and go on a rampage.
hunks.sol: If he’d seen this, he would’ve blurted out something like, *Wow! I’ve never heard the greatest assassin of all time swear before!* Then we’d have had to watch the greatest assassin of all time lose his mind.

hunks.baseline: Fortunately, the man with another identity as the Divine Physician knew how to keep to a minimum standard of decency—unlike my dear Master—and, as a former assassin, had a near-supernatural skill for recovering his composure.
hunks.sol: Fortunately, unlike my dear Master, the man who was also the Divine Physician knew where to draw the line. And as a former assassin, he had an almost supernatural talent for regaining his composure.

hunks.baseline: “Fine. Sure… I can understand that. People close to a patient sometimes can’t make sound judgments. That happens. I get it.”
hunks.sol: “Fine. Yes… It happens. People close to a patient sometimes can’t think clearly. It happens. I understand.”

hunks.baseline: After muttering as if trying to hypnotize himself, the Slaughter Saint took a steadying breath and turned to me.
hunks.sol: Muttering to himself as if under hypnosis, the Slaughter Saint steadied his breathing and turned to me.

hunks.baseline: Then, with a suddenness I could never have predicted, he blurted out a question.
hunks.sol: Then he asked something I could never have anticipated.

hunks.baseline: “Your hometown. I heard you called it the realm of immortals?”
hunks.sol: “Your hometown. The realm of immortals, wasn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: For just a moment, it felt as though the world had stopped.
hunks.sol: For a moment, the world seemed to stop.

hunks.baseline: If not for the carriage’s constant rattling, the sand slipping through the window, and Jeok Cheongang’s extremely deliberate clearing of his throat, I might’ve believed it had.
hunks.sol: If not for the carriage’s constant rattling, the sand slipping through the window, and Jeok Cheongang’s conspicuously deliberate clearing of his throat, I might have believed it had.

hunks.baseline: “Ahem. It came up.”
hunks.sol: “Ahem. Well, that happened.”

hunks.baseline: *It came up. It came up. It came up…*
hunks.sol: *That happened. That happened. That happened…*

hunks.baseline: His voice echoed like an echo, though we weren’t in some deep mountain valley. I closed my eyes for a moment, then opened them.
hunks.sol: His words echoed in my head, though we weren’t standing in some deep mountain valley. I closed my eyes for a moment, then opened them and looked at Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang was trying very hard to look stern.
hunks.sol: He was trying very hard to look stern.

hunks.baseline: I gazed at him in silence.
hunks.sol: I said nothing. I just kept looking at him.

hunks.baseline: “Well, I couldn’t help it. You’d been out cold for a whole month, and I was worried. The Slaughter Saint kept asking questions…”
hunks.sol: “Well, I couldn’t help it. You’d been out cold for a whole month. I was worried, and the Slaughter Saint kept getting suspicious…”

hunks.baseline: “I explained a little. Just a little! He’s a physician. If he asks about a patient’s condition, shouldn’t he know at least something?”
hunks.sol: “I only explained a little! Just a little! He’s a physician. When he asks about a patient, he ought to know *something* about the patient’s condition!”

hunks.baseline: I let out a long sigh at Jeok Cheongang’s halting excuses.
hunks.sol: I let out a long sigh at his halting excuses.

hunks.baseline: “Understood.”
hunks.sol: “I understand.”

hunks.baseline: “You used to wake up after a few days at most, but when you stayed out this long, I started wondering if you’d been poisoned by some kind of sleeping drug from the demonic, heterodox arts… What?”
hunks.sol: “You’d always woken up after a few days at most. This time, I even wondered if you’d been poisoned with some sleeping drug from the demonic, heterodox arts… What did you say?”

hunks.baseline: Maybe it was just me, but I’d grown pretty close to the Slaughter Saint. He was one of my most dependable allies.
hunks.sol: Maybe it was just me, but I’d grown pretty close to the Slaughter Saint. He was one of my most dependable allies, too. He deserved to know my secret.

hunks.baseline: He deserved to know my secret.
hunks.sol: To be honest, part of me was relieved it was out.

hunks.baseline: Besides, the decision had been made by none other than my Master, Jeok Cheongang. He must’ve had his reasons and circumstances.

hunks.baseline: If Jeok Cheongang had slept for an entire month like a bear hibernating through winter, even I would’ve started to wonder.

hunks.baseline: Anyway…
hunks.sol: Come to think of it…

hunks.baseline: Why did I suddenly feel so cold?
hunks.sol: Why did I suddenly feel a chill?

hunks.baseline: I’d only asked in case I needed to explain more, but Jeok Cheongang hesitated, glancing at me before continuing.
hunks.sol: I’d only asked in case I needed to fill in the details, but Jeok Cheongang hesitated and glanced at me before answering.

hunks.baseline: “I told him more or less what I knew. At first, their reactions varied, but they all believed me.”
hunks.sol: “I told them more or less what I knew. Their reactions varied at first, but they all believed me.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, that’s fine. I was planning to tell you soon anyway… Wait, ‘their reactions’?”
hunks.sol: “Oh, that’s fine. I was planning to tell him soon anyway… Wait. Their reactions varied?”

hunks.baseline: There was only one of him. Why were there several reactions?
hunks.sol: There was only one of him. How could there be several reactions?

hunks.baseline: The question that flashed through my mind was answered by a shout from somewhere in the distance.
hunks.sol: A shout from somewhere in the distance answered my question.
